questions.q: The prompt is root@bazaar-server:/srv/bazaar#. What does the # tell you?
options: You are the administrator (root); be careful
questions.explain: A normal user's prompt ends with $; root's ends with #. Root can change or delete anything.

questions.q: You type rm summer sale.txt. What does rm receive?
questions.explain: The shell splits words at spaces before rm runs. Quote the name: rm "summer sale.txt".

questions.q: Who turns logs/*.log into a list of file names?
options: The shell, before the program even starts
questions.explain: Globbing is done by the shell. The program only sees the final file names, so it can't warn you about a wrong *.

questions.q: SALE=diwali. What does echo 'sale is $SALE' print?
questions.explain: Single quotes expand nothing. Double quotes ("sale is $SALE") would print sale is diwali.

questions.q: SALE = diwali prints "SALE: command not found". Why?
options: With spaces around =, the shell runs a command called SALE with arguments = and diwali
questions.explain: Variable assignment must have no spaces: SALE=diwali.

questions.q: A deploy script does cd /srv/bazaar; git pull. The folder doesn't exist. What happens?
options: cd fails, and git pull still runs, in whatever folder the script was in
questions.explain: ; runs the next command no matter what. Use && (or set -e) so a failure stops the steps that depend on it.

questions.q: In a script, BUILD_DIR is empty. What does rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR/" become?
options: rm -rf / : it tries to delete everything
questions.explain: An empty variable disappears and leaves just /. Use set -u, check [ -n "$BUILD_DIR" ], and echo destructive commands first.

questions.q: ./deploy.sh says "Permission denied" and $? is 126. What's the fix?
options: Run it as a different user
chmod +x deploy.sh (or run it with bash deploy.sh)
questions.explain: 126 means found but not executable. chmod +x marks the file as executable; bash deploy.sh asks bash to read it instead.
